_notes: Example args for workflows/research-proof.js. Keys starting with _ are ignored by the workflow.
Everything here is a placeholder for a FICTIONAL video. Replace paths, the narration and the groups with your own.
One group = one capture agent + one independent verifier. Split groups by topic in narration order (3 to 7 groups is typical);
each scope lists the exact claims (quoted) and what to capture. The REA pack used four groups: the repo itself, tools and concepts,
the devices/apps/services named, and the closing claims.
title: Tally
creator: Alex
topic: A tutorial about Tally, a fictional open-source CLI that audits a codebase, and how to rebuild one of its features yourself.
narration:
0:00 This new open-source project called Tally lets you audit any codebase
0:12 and it's completely free
3:40 the company behind the original made over 20 billion last year
7:05 you can resell whatever you build with it

groups.scope:
The Tally repo itself ("This new open-source project called Tally"; "you can resell whatever you build with it").
- Find the official repo and capture: the header (name, owner, description, stars, forks, license), the README intro, the install steps, the license file and any disclaimer.
- Record exact counts from the public API next to the screenshot (counts move by the minute).
- Save a capabilities.json summarising what the README says it can do, with sources, for a 'what it can do' visual.

"and it's completely free": the vendor's pricing page and FAQ. Capture the price, any launch vs regular price, whether a free plan or trial exists (quote the FAQ), and the terms clause on reselling or rebranding if there is one.

"the company behind the original made over 20 billion last year": the company's official annual report or investor-relations release; give the exact figure, the fiscal year and the currency.
"this is my community": the creator's community, a public post or the feed, never its price, checkout or join page.

honesty_notes: A license covers the software it ships with, not things you build by studying another app; quote the disclaimer if there is one.
Rounded revenue figures are fine as said; show the exact figure and fiscal year on screen.
privacy_rules: The creator's paid community: never capture its price or join page as a best visual.
browsing_notes: Some vendor sites block headless Chrome: render their official PDF pages instead and say so in method.

made_graphics.spec: A clean break-even table: monthly cost vs payout at 10K, 50K and 100K views per video, from the verified rates only; label growth assumptions as assumptions.
